title: Laundering dusters and cloths between routes
audience: Cleaners who launder their own dusters and cloths between routes.
learningOutcomes: Wash microfiber dusters and cloths at the dose the label gives, working them by hand.
Clean a static duster by submerging its head and spinning off the water.
Keep cloths from different zones apart so that none crosses between zones.

instruction.heading: Why cloth care matters
instruction.body: A dirty duster does not remove dust. It moves dust from one surface to the next. Clean dusters and cloths after each route so that the next surfaces are not contaminated. Keep cloths for different zones apart, so a cloth used in a washroom never reaches a desk.

instruction.heading: Washing by hand
instruction.body: Half-fill a bucket with warm water, then add a neutral cleaner or laundry detergent at the dose the label gives. Push the sleeves and cloths through the solution with your hands. Remove each one, rinse it in clean warm water, and squeeze out the water. For a static duster, submerge the head, lift it and move it up and down gently, then squeeze and spin off the water before hanging it by the handle.

instruction.heading: Drying and storing
instruction.body: Dry cloths and duster sleeves fully before you store them, since damp fibres can develop an odour. Fold microfiber cloths in quarters while in use, and store clean ones in a clean container away from chemicals.

procedure: Collect used dusters and cloths into the basket for their zone.
Half-fill the bucket with warm water, then add the dose the label gives.
Push the items through the solution with your hands.
Rinse each item, squeeze it, and hang it up.
Static dusters: submerge the head, lift and move it gently, spin off the water, and hang by the handle.
Dry fully before storing, and keep each zone's cloths in their own place.

workedExamples.situation: At the end of a dusting route, a duster that was used in a washroom is about to be used on a desk.
workedExamples.reasoning: Take the duster out of use for desks. It goes to the washroom laundry set, and a clean duster is used on the desk. Note the crossover on the job sheet for the supervisor, because it means the zone rule was broken.

equipmentAndPpe: Laundry detergent or neutral cleaner, at the label dose
Labelled laundry baskets for each zone

commonErrors.error: Storing cloths damp in a sealed bag.
commonErrors.prevention: Dry and hang cloths before they are stored.

commonErrors.error: Putting washroom cloths and dusting cloths into one basket.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep a separate basket for each zone.

commonErrors.error: Using more detergent than the label gives.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure the dose the label gives, every time.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wear gloves when handling used cloths, especially those from washrooms.
Do not mix chemicals in the wash bucket. Use only the product the site approves.

qualityStandard: Cloths are clean, rinsed and fully dry before storage.
No detergent residue is left on the cloths.
documentationEvidence: Laundry or cloth-change record, where the site requires one.
summary: A dirty duster spreads dust, so clean dusters and cloths after every route.
Wash at the label dose, rinse, squeeze, and dry fully before storage.
Keep each zone's cloths in their own basket and never cross them.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why do dusters need cleaning after each route?
options: Because a dirty duster spreads dust instead of removing it
Because dusters lose their colour and the colour fades in the sun
Because clients prefer the smell of a wet cloth

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must cloths be fully dry before they are stored?
options: Damp fibres can develop an odour
Dry cloths weigh much less in store

knowledgeChecks.question: A cloth used in a washroom is about to be used on a desk. What should happen?
options: Use it on the desk and rinse it later and then use it again
Keep it in its own zone and use a cloth from the desk set
Mix it with the desk cloths in one basket for the day
